answer: Proof-of-capacity mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to allocate cryptographic tables across ferrous storage media. A consensus beacon acts as an auditing lantern, issuing timed challenges to verify data retention over a rolling epoch horizon. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of provisioning dedicated physical disk capacity per identity, as shared storage fails lookup deadlines. However, plotting demands heavy initial compute and penalizes lightweight devices.
